items.title: HarperCollins is betting big on AI Audiobooks
items.excerpt: HarperCollins is using its ElevenLabs partnership to synthesise narration for foreign-language editions and deep-backlist titles that would never justify a studio booking, while insisting human narrators stay the standard for lead releases. It is the clearest picture yet of where a Big Five house draws the line between AI voice and cast voice.

items.title: New BISG Head Lays Out Priorities
items.excerpt: Incoming BISG executive director Allison Belan says AI 'was the first thing that came up in virtually every conversation' with members and now tops the standards body's agenda. A second industry-wide AI survey lands in fall 2026, aimed at pushing publishers from debate to concrete implementation.

items.title: Applications Still Open for Korea's Asian Publishers Week 2026
items.excerpt: The Korea Publishers Society has extended applications for Asian Publishers Week (Seoul, November 3-6), themed 'Publishing in the Era of AI: Between Crisis and Opportunity.' It is the region's biggest scheduled forum on how AI is reshaping editorial, rights and production practice across Asian markets.

items.title: The Published Voice: Whose Voice Are We Really Reading?
items.excerpt: Roohi Ghosh argues that once AI sits in the revision loop, 'author voice' stops being a stable idea — the lines between native and non-native writing blur, and the machine becomes another participant in the published voice of a paper. A craft question with direct consequences for editors, copyeditors and disclosure policy.

items.title: Around the Book World: August 3, 2026
items.excerpt: Andrew Albanese's roundup notes that South Korean readers in their 20s and 30s — the country's heaviest AI users — are driving a reading revival, with one reader saying 'people are using AI so much that they're losing time to read and think.' Also covers Hachette's expected windfall from the approved Anthropic settlement.

items.title: I Turned My Novel Into an AI Film, Here's How I Did It
items.excerpt: Jason Hamilton walks through his full pipeline for adapting his own novel into an AI-generated film — scripting, character consistency, shot generation and edit — as a marketing and IP-extension play for indie authors. A concrete look at where book craft meets generative video production.

items.title: 'Clarity of Thought and Responsibility': Can the Pope Move the Needle on AI Regulation?
items.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV's May encyclical on artificial intelligence is drawing unusual praise across the book trade for its argument that AI must stay human-centred and be brought under real regulatory oversight. Publishing bodies are now citing it as moral cover in licensing and training-data fights.

items.title: The New Manhattan Project: PW Talks with Kevin Roose
items.excerpt: Kevin Roose discusses 'The AGI Chronicles,' his reported book on the race to artificial general intelligence, including his access to figures like Anthropic's Dario Amodei. He argues the window for governments to set rules is closing faster than the publishing calendar can keep up with.

items.title: Guest Post — The Third Time is NOT the Charm: Who Will Own How AI Participates in Scholarship?
items.excerpt: Wendy Queen and Jonathan Woahn note the scholarly community has twice built the foundational layer only to watch commercial platforms own what sat on top of it. AI participation in scholarship is the third chance — and the terms have to be set collaboratively before the layer hardens.
